text:
Shabana Mahmood will set out plans to tackle the “corrosive and growing perception” of two-tier policing in a speech to police chiefs on Wednesday.
The home secretary will say “misguided attempts at course correction” can lead to “differential treatment” while also warning officers against engaging with “activist groups”.
Mahmood will announce that a new “impartiality standard” is being developed to ensure all members of the public are treated equally. This is intended to bring guidance on key impartiality principles into one place and aim to give police more confidence in how they handle cases, regardless of someone’s race, faith or other characteristics, and to give the public confidence they will be treated fairly.
Addressing chief constables and police and crime commissioners, Mahmood will say: “We must tackle, head-on, the corrosive and growing perception of two-tier policing in this country.
“Now let me be clear: I know the vast majority of officers police impartially and that policing without fear or favour is their creed. But there have been examples of differential treatment and they have harmed policing, allowing people – often motivated actors – to whip up the idea that there is two-tier policing in this country.”
The home secretary’s remarks come after the murder of Henry Nowak prompted criticism of alleged two-tier policing in the UK. Nowak, who was fatally stabbed by Vickrum Digwa in December 2025, was handcuffed by police as he lay dying after his attacker falsely accused him of racial abuse.
The Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, subsequently delivered an emergency address calling for the public to respond with “pure cold rage” and demanding an end to what he described as “two-tier policing”.
A third of Britons believed police treat people from minority ethnic backgrounds more favourably than white people, a More in Common poll found this year, noting this marked a doubling in the last two years.
On Wednesday Mahmood will tell the National Police Chiefs’ Council (NPCC) that it is “shameful”, 33 years after the murder of the black teenager Stephen Lawrence, that the proportion of black officers remains virtually unchanged.
But Mahmood will argue that some approaches intended to promote equality, such as the former police anti-racism commitment, have risked undermining confidence in impartial policing. “We must also be wary of misguided attempts at course correction, where the pursuit of equality leads instead to differential treatment,” she is to say. “To the public, it was patently absurd to tell police officers that fair policing does not mean treating everyone the same.”
The new standard, to be developed by the College of Policing and subject to consultation next year, will also give officers guidance on scenarios such as wearing symbols on badges and lanyards, and advise them how to behave at community-led events.
Mahmood will urge officers to avoid becoming drawn into political activism. She will say: “Community engagement should mean going to a residents’ association meeting and discussing local issues. It can be over tea and biscuits, or tea and samosas, but it doesn’t mean engaging with activist groups and campaigners who are pushing an agenda and not representing a community.
“Leave the politics to the politicians – and we will leave the policing to you.”
Mahmood will also set out plans to fast-track talented recruits – including from outside policing – to senior ranks to address sometimes “inadequate” leadership.
Gavin Stephens, the chair of the NPCC, said: “Public trust depends on the police being seen to act fairly and impartially. Barriers to justice remain, discrimination still exists within our own ranks, and we rely on the trust and confidence of all communities to do our job. A diverse service is a stronger service.
“Equally, there have been occasions where well-intentioned approaches and our language have led some people to question whether policing has remained focused on its core purpose. We should take those concerns seriously.”
digest_he:
שרת הפנים של בריטניה, שבנה מחמוד, צפויה להציג בוועידת ראשי המשטרה תוכנית רחבה שמטרתה להתמודד עם התפיסה הציבורית הגוברת בדבר קיומו של שיטור דו-מסלולי במדינה. השרה תזהיר מפני ניסיונות מוטעים לתיקון קורסים העלולים להוביל ליחס דיפרנציאלי כלפי אזרחים, ותדגיש את החשיבות של שמירה על שוויון בפני החוק ללא קשר לגזע או לאמונה. במסגרת זו, יושק תקן אי-תלות חדש שנועד לאחד הנחיות מרכזיות ולחזק את אמון הציבור והשוטרים כאחד.

הכרזה זו מגיעה בעקבות שורה של אירועים ומחלוקות ציבוריות שעוררו ביקורת חריפה על תפקוד כוחות האכיפה, כולל מקרים שזכו לתשומת לב תקשורתית רבה וגרמו לטענות על אפליה. השרה מחמוד תדגיש כי למרות שרוב שוטרי המדינה פועלים בצורה הוגנת וללא משוא פנים, יש למגר מקרים חריגים שפגעו באמון הציבור. בנוסף, התוכנית תכלול הנחיות ברורות כיצד על שוטרים להימנע ממעורבות בפעילות פוליטית או ציבורית שאינה עולה בקנה אחד עם תפקידם הנייטרלי.
